proposed_assumption.label: ass:uniform-poly-time-model
proposed_assumption.statement: Fix the following computational conventions, used for every complexity claim in this paper. (i) Canonical carrier and encoding: for a finite simple bow-free ADMG G on vertex set U with |U| = n, singleton target s, and positive rational cost c, the supplied total order on U induces the order isomorphism U \simeq \mathrm{Fin}\,n; the instance is encoded as the resulting \mathrm{Fin}\,n-carrier tuple (directed and bidirected adjacency bit-matrices, the index of s, and the numerators and denominators of c in binary), of encoding length L = \mathrm{poly}(n, \mathrm{bitlen}(c)). Every statement of the form 'X is computable in polynomial time' means: the induced map on canonically encoded \mathrm{Fin}\,n instances is computable in time polynomial in (n, L). (ii) Relabeling invariance: all predicates and objective values appearing in this paper (\mathcal C(G,s), r(G,s), \mathrm{LP}(G,s,c), \mathrm{OPT}(G,s,c), feasibility of an intervention set) are invariant under vertex relabeling, so a polynomial-time algorithm on the canonical \mathrm{Fin}\,n carrier transfers to any finite vertex type U via the supplied order, with the transfer costing polynomial overhead. (iii) Elementary-count translation: an algorithm performing \mathrm{poly}(n, L) elementary operations on encoded instances (graph adjacency queries, reachability and ancestor searches, comparisons and field operations on rationals of bit length \mathrm{poly}(L)) runs in time \mathrm{poly}(n, L). (iv) Closure under guarded composition: the class of polynomial-time maps on canonically encoded instances is closed under composition, in particular the composition of the private-guard expansion, the parent-spouse rounding, and the reverse guard-replacement map is polynomial time.
proposed_assumption.source: Standard, universally accepted conventions of the polynomial-time model (Cobham-Edmonds thesis; closure of FP under composition; encoding-independence up to polynomial reencoding). They fix the ambient computational model the draft already presupposes and are formally necessary here only because Mathlib's `Turing.TM2ComputableInPolyTime` is monomorphic in its function and encoders and its composition lemma `Turing.TM2ComputableInPolyTime.comp` exists only as `proof_wanted`. They constrain no graph, cost, or rank; the kernel claims — the first nonempty rank boundary, the exact weighted natural-LP gap at rank three, and the UGC-conditional (2-epsilon) threshold on the sparse subclass — are untouched.

assumption_classifications.label: ass:uniform-poly-time-model
assumption_classifications.one_line: The draft already asserts polynomial-time algorithms and a polynomial guard-replacement reduction without ever fixing a machine model, an instance encoding, or composition closure — without these the .tex's own 'polynomial time' predicate over an arbitrary vertex type U is not a well-defined object, so writing them down is rigor the proposer owed at Stage -1, not a restriction of the rank-three/2-epsilon frontier that is the headline claim.

review.verbatim_critique: [D0.5.G cold referee] delivered tier=subfield below novelty_target=field (floor=field). The proved algorithmic frontier is promise-based: the factor-two algorithm and exact LP-gap result require r(G,s) <= 3, while recognizing that promise on an arbitrary input remains open. The unconditional lower results are NP/APX hardness; the matching (2-epsilon) approximation threshold is conditional on UGC and established through the narrower unit-cost private-guard subclass. The causal-identification interpretation relies on the imported hedge-hitting equivalence, and the package provides no solver benchmarks demonstrating the asserted benefit to the named RC2/Gurobi workflows. The framing accurately states these restrictions, but their narrow combinatorial scope and the absence of practical evidence constrain the leading-econometrics-journal score.
